evidence.note: Claim: commit_shards commits the event shards to the primary checkout's current HEAD, so a door that runs while that checkout is on an item branch (release fix-B-complete-refusal-contradicts-approval-advice, reflog main->branch->main) committed 27 events onto the item branch, stranding them off main (Baa48528523). Mechanism: the release door calls commit_at->commit_shards(log.root=primary) which builds the private index on HEAD and git-commits to HEAD. Refutation: if refusing were wrong, the off-default refusal note would never fire. Cheapest test: tests/test_eventcommit_off_default.py::test_commit_shards_refuses_off_the_default_branch -- against UNFIXED code it FAILED (AssertionError: commit sha returned on the item branch), against FIXED code it passed. Verdict: CONFIRMED.

Implemented in ddflow/services/eventcommit.py: a new _off_default() helper + stop() refusal in _read_plan. commit_shards now returns early with a note when HEAD is on a non-default branch, leaving the events for the next door on the default branch, so a release/merge/complete/stop never strands them off main. Regression test tests/test_eventcommit_off_default.py (2 tests) added; fails on unfixed code, passes fixed.

chunk_findings.detail: `_off_default` treats a failed `symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD` as safe and returns `""`, so `commit_shards` still commits. On a detached HEAD (including detached at `main`), that commit does not update `refs/heads/<default>`, so the events exist only as an unreferenced sha. Checking out or cloning the default branch drops them the same way Baa48528523 drops a commit parked on an item branch; `git gc` can delete them. Input: shards uncommitted, `git checkout --detach`, then `commit_shards` — it records a sha instead of refusing.

chunk_findings.detail: When `default_branch` returns `"HEAD"`, the guard also returns `""` and allows the commit. Input: no resolvable default branch, HEAD on `refs/heads/item`, uncommitted shards — `commit_shards` lands the events commit on `item`. Deleting that branch loses them, which is the failure the guard is supposed to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eventcommit.py:137

data.probe: default_branch resolves from the same HEAD the guard reads: when HEAD is on refs/heads/item with no origin/HEAD or main/master, default_branch returns 'item' (its rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD fallback), never 'HEAD'; 'HEAD' is returned only for a detached HEAD, which the guard refuses, not allows. The premise 'default_branch returns HEAD with HEAD on refs/heads/item' cannot hold.

chunk_findings.detail: `commit_shards` now returns `stop` whenever HEAD is not `refs/heads/<default>`, and this change never checks out the default branch or commits there. The Baa48528523 door appends the release events and calls `commit_shards` once while the primary checkout is on the item branch, then switches back to main: given that input, `sha` is empty, the events are not on `main`, and the only recovery in the new test is a second `commit_shards` after `checkout main` that production does not do. The guard also runs before any dirty-shard check, so the same call with `uncommitted_shards(repo)==[]` (door on `item`, nothing to record) is a failure instead of a no-op, which aborts that release even when it cannot strand an event commit.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous HIGH still stands: `_off_default` only makes `commit_shards` return `stop` when HEAD is not `refs/heads/<default>`, and nothing in this change checks out the default branch or commits the release events there. Baa48528523's door appends the release events and calls `commit_shards` once while the primary checkout is on the item branch, then switches back to main. On that input `sha` is empty and the events are not on `main`. The new test's recovery is a second `commit_shards` after `checkout main`, which production does not do, so the release is still not recorded on main and deleting the item branch (or a later door that never runs on the default branch) can still lose the events the shard-marks already counted.

Baa48528523's door appends the release events and calls `commit_shards` once while the primary checkout is on the item branch, then switches back to main. On that input `sha` is empty and the events are not on `main`. On a detached HEAD (including detached at `main`), that commit does not update `refs/heads/<default>`, so the events exist only as an unreferenced sha. Checking out or cloning the default branch drops them the same way Baa48528523 drops a commit parked on an item branch; `git gc` can delete them.
